data.name: Muscle growth
data.description: mTORC1-dependent process of skeletal muscle fiber enlargement (hypertrophy); driven by growth factors and exercise, blocked by rapamycin.
data.description_beginner: The process by which muscle fibers get bigger (hypertrophy), driven by exercise and growth signals and requiring mTORC1 activity. Blocking mTORC1 blocks this growth response.

studies.title: Rapamycin administration in humans blocks the contraction-induced increase in skeletal muscle protein synthesis
studies.authors: Drummond MJ; Rasmussen BB et al.

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Rapamycin given before resistance exercise completely blocked the normal post-exercise increase in human muscle protein synthesis.

studies.title: Influence of rapamycin on safety and healthspan metrics after one year: PEARL trial results
studies.authors: Moel M; Harinath G; Lee V; Nyquist A; Morgan SL; Isman A; Zalzala S

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: First completed long-term RCT of rapamycin for healthy human aging (NCT04488601, 48 weeks, n=114). Primary endpoint (visceral fat by DXA) showed NO significant change (p=0.942) - a null result on the pre-registered primary endpoint. Secondary endpoints were more promising: women on the 10mg/week dose had significant improvements in lean tissue mass and self-reported pain. A textbook example of why the pre-registered primary endpoint, not the most exciting secondary finding, is what should drive the headline conclusion.

studies.title: Mediation of IGF-1-induced skeletal myotube hypertrophy by PI(3)K/Akt/mTOR and PI(3)K/Akt/GSK3 pathways
studies.authors: Rommel C; Bodine SC et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Shows IGF-1 drives muscle fiber hypertrophy through Akt, via both the mTOR and GSK3 branches, in cultured myotubes, establishing mTOR as a central node for muscle growth signaling.

relations.mechanism: Sustained cap-dependent translation is what physically builds muscle. Blocking mTOR in humans blunts the protein-synthesis response to exercise.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Ongoing protein-building is what physically builds muscle – and in people, blocking mTOR blunts the rise in muscle protein-building after a single bout of exercise. That is the measurement that exists; how much muscle is gained over months under the drug was not measured.
relations.context: Requires mechanical load. mTORC1 activation without loading does not reproduce healthy hypertrophy, and constitutive activation alone is not sufficient.
relations.boundary: DRU2009 is direct human evidence: rapamycin blocked the contraction-induced rise in muscle protein synthesis in volunteers.
